startup: export PATH=/home/container/.local/bin:$PATH; if [[ "{{AUTO_UPDATE}}" == "1" ]]; then echo "Updating Red-DiscordBot..."; python -m pip install --user --upgrade --no-warn-script-location Red-DiscordBot; fi; redbot "{{INSTANCE_NAME}}" --no-prompt --token "{{BOT_TOKEN}}" --prefix "{{BOT_PREFIX}}"

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Red-DiscordBot installation
#
# Server files: /mnt/server at install time, /home/container at run time.

set -euo pipefail

INSTANCE_NAME="${INSTANCE_NAME:-velrix}"

# -qq plus noninteractive: apt's per-package Unpacking/Setting up chatter was
# two thirds of this log. Errors still print, which is the only part anyone
# reads an install log for.
echo "Installing prerequisites..."
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
apt-get -qq update
apt-get -qq install -y --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates

# No build-essential. Every Red dependency resolves to a prebuilt wheel on
# x86-64, verified by a full install logging zero source builds, so a compiler
# is a large download and ~250 log lines that nothing uses. If pip ever starts
# reporting "Building wheel for ..." here -- a new dependency without a wheel,
# or a non-x86-64 node -- add build-essential back to the line above.

# The volume is mounted at /mnt/server during install and /home/container when
# the server runs. Red records ABSOLUTE paths in two places that outlive this
# script -- the instance's data path, and the console-script shebangs pip writes
# into .local/bin -- so installing against /mnt/server produces a bot that
# cannot find itself on first boot.
#
# Symlinking the runtime path onto the volume makes every path Red writes down
# already correct. Files land in /mnt/server; the paths recorded say
# /home/container; at run time that IS the same directory.
mkdir -p /mnt/server
if [ ! -L /home/container ]; then
    rm -rf /home/container
    ln -s /mnt/server /home/container
fi

export HOME=/home/container
export PATH="${HOME}/.local/bin:${PATH}"
cd "${HOME}"

# --user rather than a venv: a venv hardcodes its own path in every script and
# in pyvenv.cfg, while --user installs resolve against $HOME at run time, which
# is exactly the thing that differs between these two containers.
#
# The install image is the same python:3.11-slim-bookworm the runtime yolk is
# built from, so the interpreter path baked into console scripts
# (/usr/local/bin/python) and the site-packages directory (python3.11) are
# identical on both sides. Changing either image without the other breaks that.
# --root-user-action=ignore: the installer container IS root by design, so pip's
# "don't run me as root" warning is advice for a situation that cannot arise
# here, and it is four lines of red in every install log.
# --progress-bar off: nothing reads this log while it streams, so the bars are
# just wrapped noise in the saved output.
PIP_FLAGS="--user --upgrade --no-warn-script-location --root-user-action=ignore --progress-bar off"

echo "Installing Red-DiscordBot..."
python -m pip install ${PIP_FLAGS} pip wheel
python -m pip install ${PIP_FLAGS} Red-DiscordBot

# redbot-setup is a prompt-driven wizard by default and would hang forever in an
# installer with no TTY. --no-prompt makes it scriptable and requires the name.
# --overwrite-existing-instance keeps a rebuild idempotent instead of failing on
# the instance left behind by the previous install.
echo "Creating instance '${INSTANCE_NAME}'..."
redbot-setup --no-prompt \
    --instance-name "${INSTANCE_NAME}" \
    --data-path "${HOME}/data" \
    --backend json \
    --overwrite-existing-instance

mkdir -p "${HOME}/data"

# redbot-setup RESOLVES the data path before saving it, which follows the
# symlink above straight back to /mnt/server -- a directory that does not exist
# when the server boots. The files are in the right place either way; only the
# recorded string is wrong, so correct it. Verified by inspecting the written
# config: without this it reads "/mnt/server/data".
python - <<'PYFIX'
import json
import os

path = os.path.expanduser("~/.config/Red-DiscordBot/config.json")
name = os.environ["INSTANCE_NAME"]
with open(path) as handle:
    config = json.load(handle)
config[name]["DATA_PATH"] = "/home/container/data"
with open(path, "w") as handle:
    json.dump(config, handle, indent=4)
print(f"data path pinned to {config[name]['DATA_PATH']}")
PYFIX

echo "Red-DiscordBot install complete."
exit 0

variables.name: Bot Token
variables.description: Your bot's token from the Discord Developer Portal (Bot -> Reset Token). Keep it private: anyone with it controls your bot.

variables.name: Command Prefix
variables.description: What your commands start with, e.g. ! gives !help. You can change this later from inside Discord.

variables.name: Instance Name
variables.description: The name Red stores this bot's data under. Changing it after install points the bot at an empty instance, so leave it alone unless you know why you are changing it.

variables.name: Update On Boot
variables.description: Install the latest Red-DiscordBot release each time the server starts. Turn off to pin the version you have.
